newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 26.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 26.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
The ACCC has delayed its decision on the Westpac-BML merger as it seeks further concessions from Westpac, the Sydney Morning Herald reported.
A trading halt has been placed on the shares of these two companies, who are linked to the Mt Kare gold prospect in Papua New Guinea, pending an announcement.

New Zealand investor Graeme Hart has said he was behind the purchase late on Wednesday of a further 3.5 percent of troubled food group Burns Philp & Co Ltd, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Thursday.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.40 (-0.10)

A wave of speculative selling swept through the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper market on Wednesday, driving prices to the lowest levels for seven weeks. The benchmark three months delivery price fell to $2,355 a tonne at one stage during hectic trading, down $82 from Tuesday. The beleaguered market is some $230, or nine percent, down from the $2,594 high of last Friday.
WMC chief executive Hugh Morgan is to address a Securities Institute of Australia luncheon in Sydney at midday.
CIBC today announced that it has reached an agreement to sell 100 per cent of its interest in Tillsmith Systems to Keycorp Limited and that it made a C$5 million profit on the sale.
Santos Ltd said late on Wednesday it made a new pool gas discovery in the Merrimelia-Innamincka Block of the onshore Cooper Basin in South Australia.
